chapter_theme: The chapter finishes the attack on gurus made of the same blood as everyone else, rosaries and holy baths, and sectarian division (the lord of Tillai and the lord of Arangam are one, moon in his left eye and sun in his right), then turns to what Sivavakkiyar does affirm: the letters A, U and SI and the fifty-one letters held in one, the five letters Sivaya as the real bathing place and the means that calls back the departed breath, the gate (வாசல்) that must be opened for the light to appear, the light sprung in the root channel that makes one a child and Brahman, and the Lord who is not form, not space, not great, not small, and whose beginninglessness the poet turns into a question for the yogis.
structure_note: 1014 completes the antadi chain from 1013. 1017 to 1019 are the Hari-Hara verses; 1022 and 1023 handle letters, 1024 and 1025 resume the நீ catalogue of 972; 1027, 1031, 1032 and 1036 are the வாசல் (gate) verses; 1033 repeats the oath line of 968 and 986. The chapter ends mid-work at 1038, a question to the yogis matched by 1023's.

1014.reading: Becoming gurus of words, becoming bodies of light, becoming true gurus, doing the required puja, becoming sat-gurus, telling the sastras, becoming gurus of deeds: all of it is the impurity gathered and rolled.
1014.nuance: Continues 1013: the clotted menstrual blood that became the word-gurus became every other kind of guru too, so no teacher is purer than his birth. A second reading takes திரண்டுருண்ட தூமை as 'all this is so much filth', dismissing the ranks of gurus outright. சோதிமேனி (body of light) among them is striking, since 1027 holds it out as the goal.

1015.reading: Seeing hand-rosaries you stand blinking your eyes; what places do you see as you count and count? If you can look fittingly at the mind that has known falsehood, you may quickly tell it within yourselves, crossing the body.
1015.nuance: கைவடம் is the rosary and கண்சிமிட்டி the eyes closed and fluttering in japa. பொய்யுணர்ந்த சிந்தை can be the mind that knows the falseness (of these shows) or the mind that has known only falsehood and must now be looked at. மெய்கடந்து puns on மெய், body and truth.

1016.reading: As one catches a tiger by showing it a goat, will you bewilder my mind by showing me cattle? King who killed and flayed the elephant by showing the tusk: you must show me release and bring me out.
1016.nuance: மாடு is cattle and, by extension, wealth: the Lord baits the poet with worldly goods as the hunter baits the tiger. கோடு காட்டி (showing the horn or tusk) in the elephant-flaying myth is obscure; it may only keep the pattern of காட்டி in each line. வெளிப்படுத்த can be 'reveal me' or 'bring me out (of the trap)'.

1017.reading: In your left eye the moon, in your right eye the sun; in your left hand conch and discus, in your right the trident, deer and axe; the raised foot, the long crown, beyond the eight directions; who can see the marvel that stands mingled with the body?
1017.nuance: The description is of the joint Hari-Hara form, Vishnu's emblems on the left and Siva's on the right. Tradition also reads it as the body's yoga: moon and sun are the left and right breaths, and the form 'mingled with the body' (உடல் கலந்து நின்ற) is the Lord as the breath itself. மாயம் here is marvel or hidden working rather than delusion.

1018.reading: As a measure of water and a measure of salt become one measure, the ocean-hued one and Isa sit and dwell together in one place; those who speak of Isa with the river in his hair and the moving discus-bearer as different will fall into a hell for nothing.
1018.nuance: Salt dissolved in water adds no volume, a stronger figure for identity than the gold of 993. ஏறில் ஆறு ஈசன் is read as Isa with the river (ஆறு) in his hair or on his bull (ஏறு); the phrase is compressed. வீண் நரகு is a hell entered for nothing, since the division was empty.

1019.reading: The lord of Tillai is he; the one of Tiruvarangam too is he; he who became the bounded worlds and the single release. People who have teeth and a tongue divide him and delight in the telling; those who talk of one's prowess over the other will die with rotting mouths.
1019.nuance: Tillai is Chidambaram and Arangam Srirangam, the chief Saiva and Vaishnava shrines, named only to be made one. வல்லபங்கள் பேசுவார் are those who argue which god is mightier. The curse on the mouth matches the offence, which was speech.

1020.reading: Our father, our Lord, for every direction and every life; the flame that sprouts and rises within the seed that is Sakti; after the mind is clear and the Veda-temple is opened, after seeing the Father's dance, one sees the dance of all things.
1020.nuance: சத்தியான வித்து makes Sakti the seed and the Lord the flame within it, an inversion of the usual order. வேத கோயில் (the Veda-temple) is unglossed; the body, the mind or the Veda's inner meaning are all possible. அடங்கல் ஆடல் is the dance of everything, or the dance in which all is contained.

1021.reading: Perceive the fitting books within yourselves, perceiving and perceiving, and sing; standing with attachment cut, you will reach the Supreme beyond the supreme; if you cut the pride of the hateful ones within and set them in place, the light will live within you forever as kin.
1021.nuance: Line 3, செற்றமாவை யுள்ளரைச் செருக்கறுத்து, is hard: the hateful (or hatred and desire) that are within, whose pride is to be cut, or the enemies within. The first line qualifies the attack on books: books perceived within are to be sung, not thrown out.

1022.reading: What rose as awareness, came as water, entered as the seed and grew as fire: recite the letter in which five and three became one; recite, you, the name 'Rama Rama Rama'.
1022.nuance: The first two lines trace a descent, read by tradition as conception (awareness, fluid, seed, the heat of the womb) or as the elements. அஞ்சும் மூன்றும் ஒன்றதான அக்கரம் repeats the five-and-three mantra of 980 and here names it ராம, which tradition reads as cipher for the breath (see 974). போததாய் (as awareness, from போதம்) may also be 'as a bud'.

1023.reading: Did U arise within the letter A? Did U arise within the letter U? Did A and U stand without SI? You yogis free of change, you must explain this at length.
1023.nuance: A and U are the first two letters of Om; SI is the first letter of Siva and of the five letters. The question seems to be whether the pranava can stand without the Siva-letter, and the first two lines, as printed, ask the same thing twice (அவ்வு / உவ்வு); a copying slip or a deliberate puzzle. The verse asks and does not tell.

1024.reading: You are for all the kinds of virtue, you are the cosmos and the eight directions, you are for every kind of strength, you are the thought of those who seek, you are sleep, you are awareness, you are the light mingled within; your anklet-feet that cannot be forgotten, even if I forget them, dwell in me.
1024.nuance: The last line asks the feet to stay even through the poet's forgetting, so union does not rest on his remembering. The catalogue continues 972 and includes sleep and waking awareness as the Lord.

1025.reading: You are the cosmos, you are what is beyond it, you are the primal root, you are the throat, you are thought, you are the poems; the virtuous who perceive you within, with no lotus, in the straightness of the form they have taken: what sharpness their sharpness is!
1025.nuance: கண்டம் may be the throat (the Lord's dark throat) or 'the piece', the part as against the whole. புண்டரீகம் அற்று உளே (within, without the lotus) is taken as perceiving without the lotus-seats of the yogic body, that is, without a located image; or as 'in the heart-lotus'. The last line praises the knowers' keenness.

1026.reading: In the bewilderment that women with collyrium-dark eyes cast, you have lost yourselves; if you would be free of trouble, and if by a mind that has known truth you gain the knowledge that shines, you will know how to be saved and live for aeons.
1026.nuance: ஐயிறந்து is read as ஐயம் இறந்து (doubt gone) or ஐ இறந்து (having lost the self, or having passed the five). ஊழிகாலம் வாழ்வீர், living for aeons, is the Siddhar claim of a deathless body, or long life by knowledge; the verse does not separate the two.

1027.reading: You mutes bewildered by the gate where the embryo lay: if you can mark and look at the word the guru spoke, you will become a body of shining form and become celestial, and go and join him as a body of holy radiance.
1027.nuance: கரு இருந்த வாசல் is the womb, and the bewilderment is desire for it; the way out is the guru's word attended to. The verse promises a transformed body (உருவிலங்கு மேனி, திருவிளங்கு மேனி), the Siddhar goal of a body of light rather than release from body.

1028.reading: Poor ones who go seeking, saying 'we must bathe at a holy water': tell me clearly where the bathing is. After you have stayed clear within yourselves as the holy water, what is holy water is the five letters Sivaya.
1028.nuance: தீர்த்தம் is used four times and moved from river to self to mantra. தெளிந்து (clear) is both the clarity of water and of mind, the pun carrying the argument.

1029.reading: Straightening the neck and opening the good eyes wide, you people: what sin is this sin of a mouth gone slack and hanging open? The beginningless one that is in the firm seed may dwell in the letter that is no letter, having been there.
1029.nuance: The first two lines mock a posture, the straight neck and fixed stare of show-yoga, ending in a gaping mouth. Lines 3 and 4 are corrupt: எனழுத்திலோ has no sense as printed (எழுத்திலோ, 'or in the letter', fits), and the construction 'in the letterless letter' is tradition's reading of the Lord beyond the written mantra.

1030.reading: If you can perceive, as you eat and sleep, the maya you see and the elements mingled with it, then the ancient six become one, and as the pure one of the Veda that begot them, the primal root that stands as the release of the cosmos is the root.
1030.nuance: உண்டு உறங்குமாறு (in the way of eating and sleeping) places the perception in ordinary life, not in retreat. பண்டை ஆறு, the ancient six, is unglossed: the six centres, the six ends of knowledge, the six faiths or the six limbs of the Veda are all possible. The last line's grammar is loose and the reading is tentative.

1031.reading: You who pity the gate that bore you and die beyond count: you do not know the cause of the bud blooming on the plantain that put it forth. If you can open the hanging gate and look, seeking, the maya that appears will leave and the light will come and appear.
1031.nuance: ஈன்ற வாசல் (the gate that bore you) is the womb, and pitying it is lust for it. நான்ற வாசல் (the hanging gate) is tradition's term for the uvula or the door at the palate through which the breath is raised, as in Tirumanthiram 805; the plantain bud that opens (கான்ற வாழை மொட்டு) is taken as the lotus of the head or the kundalini flowering. On a plain reading the lines are about birth and a plant, and do not connect; the coded reading carries them.

1032.reading: You mutes who swing to and fro, pitying the whirling gate: you do not think of opening the whirling gate to reach the truth; after you open the whirling gate and perceive the truth, you yourselves become the truth that was inside the whirling gate.
1032.nuance: உழலும் வாசல் (the whirling or turning gate) repeats in every line; tradition takes it as the womb-gate that keeps one turning in births, and as the inner door of 1031. ஊசலாடும் (swinging) is the oscillation of the undecided mind. The last line is identity, not vision: the opener becomes what was behind the door.

1033.reading: After you have sought and held within yourselves, for four nazhigai, the light that sprouted and rose in the root channel, you may live as a child and may become the supreme Brahman; by the oath of the one who ate the poison and by the Mother's oath, this is true.
1033.nuance: மூலநாடி is the channel at the root (the base of the spine), and the light that rises in it is what tradition calls kundalini, though the verse does not use the word. நாலு நாழி is four nazhigai, about ninety-six minutes, a daily measure of practice. The two results, a child's body and Brahman-hood, are given together, as at 968.

1034.reading: When you want to stay, can you stay by wishing it? Was it to die that they created you in the earth? Worship, before you die, the five letters spoken by the unshrinking Lord; do not lose your footing taking it as a mere medicine.
1034.nuance: The second line can be a protest (surely not created only to die?) or a statement of fact. மருந்தெனப் பதம்கெடீர் is open: do not ruin your state by treating the mantra as medicine for the body alone, or, with பதம் as the word, do not corrupt the mantra; or the mantra is the medicine, so do not lose it. Compare 1036, where the five letters recall the breath.

1035.reading: Are not all fifty-one letters contained in one letter? Are not the sky-spread mantra and the four Vedas one? Within the sky-spread root five letters it sprouted; it sat as the seat of the limb-linga: Sivayam.
1035.nuance: The fifty-one letters of the Sanskrit syllabary are reduced to one, and then the five letters are made the source of the mantra and the Vedas. அங்கலிங்க பீடம் (the seat of the body-linga) places the linga in the body, as 999 took it out of stone.

1036.reading: The letter Sivayam is the letter in which Siva dwells, the true letter to trust as the means; the breath that has gone out through the doorless gate, the five letters Sivaya will call back by that means.
1036.nuance: கபாடமற்ற வாசல் (the gate with no door) is taken as the nostrils or the opening at the crown through which the breath leaves. The claim that the mantra calls the departed breath back is read by tradition as the mantra governing the breath (vaasi) in life, or as restoring life; the verse states it flatly as உபாயம், the means.

1037.reading: Not form, not space, not a thing that stands attached to one; not belonging to the gate it joins, not the other, not the absent; not great, not small, not even what is spoken; who can see the straightness that stands as the rare one?
1037.nuance: A string of denials like 973, with the gate (வாசல்) now among the things the Lord is not bound to, so even the inner door of 1031 and 1032 is not his. நேர்மை (straightness, rightness) is the poet's name for him in 1025 too.

1038.reading: Is the self beginningless? Is the not-self beginningless? Are the five senses that flowered and their objects beginningless? Are the argument-filled books and Sadasiva beginningless? Yogis who come puffed up, you must answer quickly.
1038.nuance: அனாதி is the word Siddhanta gives to the Lord, the soul and the bond alike; Sivavakkiyar runs it down the list to the senses, the disputing sastras and Sadasiva himself and demands an answer. The taunt வீக்கவந்த (come swollen) matches விகாரமற்ற at 1023, which asks the yogis the same way about the letters.

links.note: The Kural says neither shaving nor long hair is needed if one gives up what the world condemns; Sivavakkiyar says blinking at a rosary and counting places are nothing beside looking at one's own mind. Both set the inner change above the outward mark of the devotee.

Both place the moon on the left and the sun on the right: Tirumular as a breath practice, the sun's breath set on the left and the moon's on the right so the axle-pin holds a thousand years; Sivavakkiyar as the Lord's two eyes in a body mingled with the devotee's. On tradition's reading of 1017 the eyes are the two breaths, and the image is the same practice described as a form.

993 makes Vishnu and Siva one gold under two forms; 1018 makes them salt dissolved in water, one measure with no seam, and adds the penalty for dividing them, a hell entered for nothing. The second figure is the stronger: gold keeps its forms, dissolved salt has none.

Tirumular praises Siva as the One who ends the flawed birth of Vishnu, Brahma and the gods, placing Vishnu among the born below the Lord; Sivavakkiyar says the lord of Tillai and the lord of Arangam are the same he, and curses those who rank one above the other. On the reading that Sivavakkiyar's 'he' is Siva at both shrines, the two verses disagree about Vishnu's standing; if his 'he' is a Supreme beyond both names, Tirumular's hierarchy is not contradicted.

978 says those who recite the four Vedas do not know the foot of knowledge; 1021 tells its hearers to perceive the fitting books within themselves and sing. The attack is on recitation without inward perception, not on books as such, and 1021 states the condition under which they are allowed.

980 names an unreachable mantra that is five and three and promises that reciting it burns off the five great sins; 1022 repeats the five and three become one letter and names it, ராம. Read with 974, the two verses make the ராம verses part of the mantra argument rather than a Vaishnava intrusion.

Tirumular assigns the letters: A is the soul, U the supreme, MA the impurity, SI is Siva, VA the form, YA the soul; Sivavakkiyar asks whether U arose within A and whether A and U could stand without SI, and tells the yogis to explain. The question presupposes a scheme like Tirumular's and probes how its letters generate one another.

Both run the நீ catalogue, earth, sky, number and letter in 972, virtue, cosmos, strength, sleep and awareness in 1024, and both end at the feet; 972 asks to reach them, 1024 asks them to stay even when the poet forgets.

Tirumular says there are many holy waters within the heart and that those who do not bathe in them wander over hollow and height; Sivavakkiyar asks the seekers of holy waters where the bathing is, answers that it is within, and names the water as the five letters. Sivavakkiyar makes the mantra itself the tirtha; Tirumular leaves the inner waters unnamed.

Both have a door at the palate that opens: Tirumular says if the two breaths are set in the upper palate there is no Death and the door opens; Sivavakkiyar says open the hanging gate and look, and maya leaves and the light appears. Tirumular's result is a renewed body, Sivavakkiyar's the light, but on tradition's reading the gate is the same place.

1031 says that opening the hanging gate makes maya leave and the light appear; 1032 repeats the gate in every line, calls it the whirling gate, and says the one who opens it becomes the truth that was inside. Vision in one verse becomes identity in the next.

The two verses make the same promise under the same oath: 968 raises the breath from the channel to the skull and the old become children; 1033 holds the light risen in the root channel for four nazhigai and one lives as a child and becomes Brahman. Both close on the poison-eater's and the Mother's feet or oath.

Arunagirinathar asks that the breath run from the root up the pillar through the six centres to the Supreme; Sivavakkiyar says the light sprung in the root channel, held within, makes one a child and Brahman. Both start at the root (மூலம்) and rise; the Thiruppugazh ends at the dancing foot, Sivavakkiyar at a renewed body.

Tirumular says the Lord stands as the food one eats and the medicine, and has become the five letters; Sivavakkiyar tells the hearer to worship the five letters before death and not to lose footing by taking them as medicine. Both put mantra and medicine side by side; whether 1034 affirms or warns against the equation depends on the reading of மருந்தெனப் பதம்கெடீர்.

Tirumular says the fifty letters are all the Vedas and Agamas and that, once known, the fifty become the five letters; Sivavakkiyar asks whether the fifty-one letters are not held in one letter and says the mantra and the four Vedas sprouted from the root five letters. The same reduction, fifty to five to one, in both.

Tirumular says the ground at the root is நமசிவாய and that spoken it becomes வாசி, the yoga of the breath; Sivavakkiyar says the five letters Sivaya are the means that calls back the breath gone out through the doorless gate. Both bind the five letters to the breath, Tirumular by the word வாசி, Sivavakkiyar by the claim.

Both verses define the Lord by denial: 973 not Hari, not Brahma, not great, not small, beyond turiya; 1037 not form, not space, not great, not small, not even speech, and not bound to the gate. 1037 adds the poet's own cipher, the வாசல், to what the Lord is not.

Tirumular states the Siddhanta position that the soul, the Lord and the bond are each beginningless (அனாதி); Sivavakkiyar runs the same word down to the senses, the disputing books and Sadasiva and demands that the yogis say which of them it fits. The question does not deny Tirumular's claim but presses on what the word is doing when it is given to everything.

new_concepts.gloss: the gate: in Sivavakkiyar's cipher the womb-door through which one is born, the openings of the body, and the one inner door, hanging or doorless, through which the breath leaves and the Lord and the light are reached
new_concepts.label_source: Used in the verses as வாசல் (981, 1027, 1031, 1032, 1036, 1037); also declared in ch055

source_issues: 1029 line 4 reads எழுத்திலா எனழுத்திலோ; எனழுத்திலோ is corrupt (எழுத்திலோ fits the metre and sense).
1023 lines 1 and 2 both ask whether U (அவ்வு / உவ்வு) arose, within A and within U; the repetition may be a copying slip for a different letter in one line.
1018 line 3, ஏறில்ஆறு ஈசனும், and 1021 line 3, செற்றமாவை யுள்ளரைச், are obscure as printed and may be corrupt.
1014 continues 1013 antadi-fashion across the tool's chapter split.
